reconcile_requests in .warp/request_reconcile.py is a repo-only sibling of the shipped reconcile_promotions. It finds OPEN requests by the repo index (the warp.request/v1 records passed in, read from .warp/requests/ by the reference reconcile_from_repo) plus the issue link (record.tracker.issue) plus a status query (_is_open_status: a known request status that is not already terminal) and NEVER by assignee==agent (the module reads no assignee field at all). For each it pulls the ordered attributed changelog via read_changelog and derives the TRUE actor and intent FROM THE CHANGELOG: _opening_actor is the verified proposer (the actor of the opening transition, from no prior state), _terminal_decision resolves the decisive terminal transition and _entry_actors the approving actor(s), and the receipt is keyed on the terminal entry's id - never from the current status, which anyone can set or which can drift.

Any gap, conflict, or ambiguity (no attributable actor, an unresolvable proposer, both an accept and a reject terminal transition) BLOCKS - held, never inferred or defaulted-open. The frozen readers authorization.py / two_key.py / policy_check.py / decision.py are edited nowhere and carry no reference to this module.

On a validated acceptance the reconcile writes the touchpoint settlement record (warp.approval for spec_approval/plan_approval/risky_action_authorization/escalation, warp.decision for decision_choice, warp.verdict for review_disposition, binding to the recomputed digest and naming the verified actor(s), carrying the request_id and changelog_id back-reference the frozen readers tolerate) and emits the event (request.accepted, plus decision.decided for an accepted decision_choice; a rejection emits request.rejected; the event vocabulary REUSED from request.REQUEST_EVENT_TYPES so it cannot drift) ONLY through the injected SettlementStore's append-only COMPARE-AND-SWAP settle(request_id, changelog_id, record, events): it writes AT MOST ONCE per (request_id, changelog_id), so a re-run, a re-projection, or a duplicated changelog entry is a NO-OP. The repo is the single source of truth: the settlement record lands in the repo FIRST and the reconcile writes NO tracker state (the FakeTracker write audit is empty after a run); setting the terminal tracker state is the downstream W3 projection. The reference FilesystemSettlementStore writes an append-only .warp/receipts.jsonl plus the settlement record under .warp/settlements/ and appends the event to .warp/events.jsonl, wired per repo and NEVER gate-run (the FakeSettlementStore runs).
